stem: A 13-year-old girl steps on a garden fork in a vegetable patch, sustaining a deep puncture wound to her heel contaminated with soil and manure. Her records show DTPa at 2, 4 and 6 months, 18 months and 4 years, but she was absent on the Year 7 school vaccination day. She has no immune problems. What tetanus prophylaxis is recommended?

options.label: A
options.explanation: Immunoglobulin gives passive cover when active immunity is doubtful. She has had 5 doses, so TIG is not needed, and TIG alone would miss the booster she is due.

options.label: B
options.explanation: TIG is reserved for tetanus-prone wounds in people with fewer than 3 doses, an uncertain history or significant immunodeficiency. None of these applies to her.

options.label: C
options.explanation: This would be right if her last dose were under 5 years ago. Her last dose was at 4 years, about 9 years ago, so a tetanus-prone wound needs a booster.

options.label: D
options.explanation: She completed a primary course and boosters, so immunological memory is intact. One booster is enough; the course does not need restarting.

options.label: E
options.explanation: Correct. With 3 or more doses and the last over 5 years ago, a tetanus-prone wound needs a booster. From age 10, dTpa (or dT) is used; TIG is not required.

context: Tetanus-prone wound: with 3 or more prior doses, boost if the last dose was over 5 years ago; add TIG only for fewer than 3 doses, an uncertain history or immunodeficiency.
